name: Santa Fe Springs Celebration
place: Ichetucknee Springs to the Santa Fe River
included: Camping, catered breakfasts and dinners, daily lunch snacks and shuttle. Optional cabins at Bowman's Landing (Nov 6 and 7) cost extra.
cabinsNote: Rentals: Doug at Rum 138, 386-454-4247, who prefers 12 to 14 foot kayaks. Optional cabins at Bowman's Landing on Nov 6 and 7 are extra and booked separately.

overview.title: Our 100th trip, on the springs
overview.text: Crystal-clear Ichetucknee Springs, the Santa Fe River and the springs along it make this a celebration of the water Paddle Florida exists to protect. An extra day was added for our 100th multi-day trip, with a layover day at Bowman's Landing.
minis: Paddling and layover days, tent camping

days.title: Arrive and kick off
days.body: Check in from 1 to 5 PM at Ichetucknee Springs Campground and set up your tent. Dinner is at 6 PM, followed by the kickoff program and the required trip orientation.

days.title: Ichetucknee Spring Run
days.body: An up-and-back paddle on the Ichetucknee Spring Run from the park’s north entrance. Breakfast is at 7:30 AM and boats launch between 8:30 and 9. Dampiers Landing restaurant is nearby.

days.title: Ichetucknee to Lemons Memorial Park
days.body: Paddle north to Lemons Memorial Park, then settle in at Gilchrist Blue Springs State Park for two nights.

days.title: High Springs to River Rise
days.body: Launch at the High Springs boat ramp and paddle to River Rise, then back to camp at Gilchrist. Add distance if you want a longer day.

days.title: Gilchrist to Bowman's Landing
days.body: The last moving day, ending at Bowman's Landing. Optional cabins here are extra and booked separately.

days.title: Layover day
days.body: A free day. Relax, explore, or paddle up to 6 optional miles.

days.title: Breakfast and farewell
days.body: A hearty breakfast, then pack up and head home.

camps.name: Bowman's Landing
camps.note: Optional cabins for Nov 6 and 7, booked and paid separately.

boat: Sit-in kayak, sit-on-top kayak or paddleboard, at least 12 feet. Beginners are welcome, with basic paddling and swimming skills.
baggage: Two bags and 40 pounds in total. You carry them from your car to camp and back at the end. Label them with your name.
water: Non-inflatable Coast Guard-approved PFD, worn on the water
Bow line, 8 to 10 ft, secured so it cannot come loose
Grab loops at bow and stern
First aid kit in a waterproof cover
Repair kit (duct tape, sealant, waterproof tape)
Rain gear and a fleece or light jacket
Dry change of clothes in a waterproof bag
Water for the day and snacks (lunch is provided)
land: Something to read, music or earplugs
faq: Dinner at 6 PM and an evening program at 7 PM. Programs include authors, historians and environmental experts, and one night of live music.
How do I get back to my car?
Shuttle details for the end of the trip come in your confirmation email, sent 7 days before the trip with the waiver link.
Open to all skill levels. Paddlers under 18 must be with a parent or guardian, with no more than two children under 12 per adult. A signed waiver and emergency contact are required. No pets.
What are the rules on the water?
Wear a non-inflatable PFD at all times. People-powered boats only. Follow park rules, including the alcohol ban, and respect private property along the river.
All payments are non-refundable, including for weather and water levels. Paddle Florida strongly recommends buying trip cancellation insurance from an outside provider.
Yes. Final details are emailed 7 to 10 days before the trip.
